system:
You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

<sentences>
S1: The patient was instructed to discontinue use and contact the office if gastrointestinal issues develop.
S2: I have explained to him that his x-rays revealed hallux rigidus.
S3: He reports that his pain is present even with the slightest of pressure, which he notes is worse at night when his sheet is touching his right toe.
S4: He adds that he has been taking 2 ibuprofen per day, which does not provide him with relief.
S5: Skin: Reports redness.
S6: The patient states that he has been ambulating on his heel to keep his toe from bending.
S7: Right foot hallux rigidus.
S8: We discussed treatment options for this and I have recommended that we begin with conservative treatment in the form of custom orthotics.
S9: The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago, however it worsened last week.
S10: Palpated a bone spur on the right great toe.
S11: He noticed the pain worsening when he was at a trade show convention and he could not ambulate as he was forced to stand there as the pain was there the whole time.
S12: He denies any specific injury.
S13: Pain to palpation of the right great toe, between the big toe and 2nd toe.
S14: I advised the patient that I want him to continue his regular activities.
S15: Patient reports that he likes to bicycle ride.
S16: There is a loss of cartilage with some arthritis present.
S17: MSK: Examination of the right great toe reveals 10 degrees of plantar flexion with pain.
S18: Musculoskeletal: Reports right great toe pain.
S19: After reviewing the patient's examination and radiographic findings today, I have had a lengthy discussion with the patient in regards to his current symptoms.
S20: X-ray of the right great toe taken today in office reveals a large bone spur on the anterior aspect of the right great toe joint.
S21: If his pain does not improve with the orthotics, I will recommend a cortisone injection or surgical intervention.
S22: Right great toe pain.
S23: The patient describes his pain usually as throbbing and burning, but notes it occasionally changes to sharp, stabbing pain especially with movement or prolonged ambulation.
S24: I have also prescribed the patient meloxicam once a day to treat the pain.
S25: His symptoms also include redness to the right great toe.
S26: Joseph Walker is a pleasant 58-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right great toe pain.
S27: The patient will follow up with me in 2 weeks to check on his progress.
</sentences>
